subject: Procurement lane decision matrix: marketplace vs private-offer impacts for HealthSpan
messages:
From: Asha Raman <asha.raman@healthspan.io>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-01-20 09:12 -0800
Subject: Procurement path question — GCP marketplace vs private offer (co-sell implications)

Hi Jordan / team,

Quick question from Procurement as we prepare the PO for our pilot with Redwood: they want clarity on whether we should purchase through the GCP Marketplace listing (standard listing / public SKU) or go through a private-offer/direct contract route (your private offer/partner invoice flow). Key constraints they care about:
- PO number and directed invoice required by our AP team
- Timeline to have a binding price and SKUs (our FP&A needs visibility for month-end)
- Whether marketplace purchase affects Redwood partner/co-sell credits for our ISV partnerships (we have joint GTM with a systems integrator)
- Any difference in support SLAs, data residency controls, or audit evidence requests (SOC2 reports) tied to the procurement lane

Would appreciate a short matrix that helps us decide (we're leaning private-offer but want to confirm tradeoffs).

Thanks,
Asha Raman
Director, Procurement — HealthSpan

---
Attachment: HealthSpan_PO_Requirements.docx (docx, 64KB)
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Raman <asha.raman@healthspan.io>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-01-20 11:05 -0800
Subject: Re: Procurement path question — GCP marketplace vs private offer (co-sell implications)

Hi Asha — thanks for the clear list. I put together a short decision matrix and practical next steps below based on what typically breaks in enterprise procurement. TL;DR: Private-offer (direct) is usually better for PO-directed invoicing and partner credit alignment; marketplace is faster for trial usage and simplifies procurement for non-PO buyers.

Decision matrix (high level):
- Invoice & PO handling:
  - Marketplace: vendor is often billed through the cloud provider; procurement often cannot direct invoice Redwood. Good for card/CC/charge models, not ideal for directed PO + invoice routing.
  - Private offer / direct: Redwood issues directed invoice or partner invoice per the PO; supports Net terms and PO number on invoice (recommended for your AP needs).

- Price / SKU visibility & timing:
  - Marketplace: SKUs can be listed publicly and charges are visible as line items, but private-offer discounts and committed SKUs are only visible after a private offer is issued.
  - Private offer: we can lock a price and SKU mapping in the private-offer before signing — gives your FP&A the visibility they need. Estimated lead time: 3–5 business days to generate formal private-offer once terms are agreed.

- Co-sell / partner crediting:
  - Marketplace: some cloud marketplaces restrict partner co-sell crediting (depends on cloud and partner program); public marketplace purchases can make co-sell attribution more complex.
  - Private offer: straightforward to attribute partner credit and invoice through partner/reseller if required. If you're working with an SI, we can route the invoice through them or attribute credit in the private-offer metadata.

- Support SLAs & compliance evidence:
  - Marketplace: runtime support is the same, but contractual SLAs and custom terms are limited by the marketplace terms. SOC2 evidence access remains the same; however, contract-level indemnities / data residency controls are easier to negotiate in a private contract.
  - Private offer: you can request explicit contractual clauses (data residency, audit rights, SOC2 timelines) in the MSA/PO or attach an addendum. Redwood can support a VPC/private deployment in a private contract if needed.

- Billing cadence & credits:
  - Marketplace: usually monthly through cloud bill; limited options for billing cadence changes.
  - Private offer: customizable (monthly, quarterly, annual) and supports credits/offsets tied to committed spend.

Recommendation for HealthSpan (practical):
1) For the pilot where you need a PO + directed invoice and partner credit: go private-offer. We'll issue a private-offer that maps to explicit SKUs, includes your PO number on invoice, and sets partner attribution metadata.
2) For initial evaluation or a low-risk sandbox where speed matters and no PO is required: marketplace listing is fine.
3) If you need contractual controls (data residency, audit logs retention, or SOC2 addendum): private-offer / MSA route.

Next steps I propose (pick 2):
- I can generate a draft private-offer template and submit to your procurement (I attached our Private Offer template).
- Lauren and I can host a 20-minute call with your AP team to confirm PO fields and invoice routing.
- If you prefer the marketplace path, I can confirm whether your SI partner will still receive co-sell credit and provide the exact marketplace SKU IDs.

Attachments: RDW_Private_Offer_Template.pdf (pdf, 48KB)

If that aligns, I'll kick off the private-offer generation once you confirm.

—Jordan Blake
Sr. Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Asha Raman <asha.raman@healthspan.io>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-01-20 13:02 -0800
Subject: Re: Procurement path question — GCP marketplace vs private offer (co-sell implications)

Adding a quick technical note from infra/ops perspective:
- Marketplace vs private-offer does not change runtime topology for our hosted offering, but private-offer contracts are required if you want a Dedicated pool or a Private (VPC) deployment with explicit data residency.
- If HealthSpan plans to enable private KV caching or customer-managed keys (KMS), that is only available in Private deployment or in Dedicated (not via basic marketplace listing).
- For audit/evidence: SOC2 reports are available regardless; if you need longer log retention or specific tracing hooks we should capture that in the private-offer SOW.

Happy to join the AP sync for any technical clarifications.

—Karthik
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
From: Asha Raman <asha.raman@healthspan.io>

Thanks — this is very helpful. I agree private-offer sounds like the right lane for the pilot. Two quick follow-ups:
1) Can you confirm the 3–5 business day estimate to generate the private-offer once you have the PO + billing contact? We need the documented ETA for our vendor onboarding checklist.
2) Will Redwood include partner attribution metadata so our SI (Brightline Partners) receives co-sell credit?

If you can generate the draft private-offer and we schedule the 20-minute AP sync tomorrow (Thursday) at 10am PT, I can loop in our AP lead and get the PO routed immediately.

Thanks again — attaching our PO requirements doc.

Best,
Asha
